source_document.body:
Freight broker RXO said Tuesday that even though truckload spot rates have cooled in the fourth quarter, the market is not entering deflationary territory.
RXO’s ( NYSE: RXO ) linehaul rate dataset, which excludes fuel surcharges, jumped 37.9% year over year in the third quarter, to “levels not seen since peak COVID-era shipping.” So far in the fourth quarter, rate growth has slowed to plus-26.2% y/y, which is “still significantly higher than 2025 heading into peak season.”
“In Q4, the overall demand picture remains muted against an uncertain economic backdrop, but sustained pressure on the supply side of the market (carriers) has created a tight environment for shippers — and peak season is fast approaching,” the company’s Curve Report stated.
SONAR: National Truckload Index (linehaul only – NTIL.USA) for 2026 (blue shaded area), 2025 (yellow line), 2024 (green line) and 2023 (pink line). The NTIL is based on an average of booked spot dry van loads from 250,000 lanes. The NTIL is a seven-day moving average of linehaul spot rates excluding fuel. Rates remain significantly higher on a y/y comparison in November. To learn more about SONAR, click here .
SONAR: Outbound Tender Rejection Index (OTRI.USA) for 2026 (blue shaded area), 2025 (yellow line), 2024 (green line) and 2023 (pink line). A proxy for truck capacity, the tender rejection index shows the number of loads being rejected by carriers. Current tender rejections show a tight truckload market.
Strict regulatory enforcement and years of weak carrier profitability have drawn down capacity , significantly tightening the market despite flat demand.
While cost pressures dominated the headlines during the third-quarter earnings season, fleets are logging large contractual rate gains after a multiyear downturn. Knight-Swift Transportation ( NYSE: KNX ) is now targeting “at least double-digit [rate] increases” in its new bid season , which began earlier this month.
Cass Information Systems ( NASDAQ: CASS ) said Monday that linehaul contract rates (ex-fuel) were up for a 22nd straight month in October, 9.9% higher y/y. The dataset averaged rate increases of 10% in the third quarter, following a plus-6% average in the second quarter.
“The combination of federal policy enforcement, increasing insurance premiums, record-high fuel, and high interest rates has both reduced the available labor pool while making the financial barriers to entry much higher,” the RXO report said. … “As long as freight demand remains muted, there won’t be extreme market volatility, but any incremental increase in shipments could result in a very difficult market for shippers.”
SONAR: Contract Rate Change Direction (CRCD.USA). The dataset measures the average percentage difference between new and former contract base rates. Recent contract renewals are averaging 12%.
RXO’s all-in cost-per-mile index, which includes fuel surcharges, stood at 160.1 in the third quarter (indexed to a 2015 baseline). This is the highest reading since the 2022 first quarter. Diesel fuel prices were up 48% y/y in the quarter, but the report said diesel didn’t account for all the rate increase.
“A substantially higher cost structure has moved the baseline up for carriers, regardless of fuel costs.”
Why it matters? Driven by tightening capacity and higher operating costs, these rate trends signal a shift in market power toward carriers seeking margin improvement. Shippers should respond by securing dependable capacity and guarding against routing guide deterioration.
